A_teardown.note: outer job A kept open -> KILL_ON_CLOSE not yet fired; only the watchdog can kill the worker here

B_teardown.note: KILL_ON_CLOSE -> host + worker + watchdog die together

required_for_PASS: A/B host assigned to the outer job
A: owner terminated + outer job kept open -> worker died + host dead (the watchdog, a surviving member, reaped the worker)
B: outer job closed -> host + worker + watchdog all died together
finding_inherited_membership: on this build, a host assigned to the outer job POST-creation does not auto-contain the children it later spawns (inherited_membership for the worker + watchdog is False) -- a process created outside the job carries an empty creation-time job chain. Genuine containment therefore requires the containing supervisor to put each already-running member into the job, which is what the explicit_child_assign step models.
note: two-phase host (assign, then spawn) + explicit containment of all three (IsProcessInJob-verified); owner-termination left the outer job open so the watchdog reaped the worker, and closing the outer job killed the whole contained subtree
